name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,901

clue.text: Squeeze Mike Pence in hearts and spades

indicators.note: putting one thing in another buries it, so the pair of letters lands within the word named next rather than beside it

blocks.note: the heart of a matter is its core, and these letters split open after the first two
Mike is how the radio alphabet says M
p is pence on any British price tag
S is the bridge scorecard's letter for spades

explanation.walkthrough: The vice-president is a decoy assembled out of a radio-alphabet letter and a coin, and only one of the two card suits in the surface is really being used as a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeeze -> COMPRESS: to compress is to force something into a smaller space, which is the plain physical sense both verbs share.

clue.text: Total calculated wrongly then correctly

indicators.note: 'then' is what happens next, so the second chunk is written after the first rather than around it

blocks.note: a sum that has gone astray is out — your figures are out by a mile
to get it correctly is to get it right

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are verdicts on a sum, which is what keeps the surface in the accounts office; the definition is doing arithmetic duty too, and is the one word that isn't.
explanation.definitionFit: Total -> OUTRIGHT: an outright lie is a total one, the adjective meaning complete and unqualified rather than fastest or first.

clue.text: Temperature to the north rising, say

indicators.note: what rises in a down entry climbs towards the top, so the letters just assembled are read from the bottom back

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation on every thermometer and weather chart
north is the top of the map, so it is up

explanation.walkthrough: A three-letter down entry offers very little to grip, so the give-away is 'say' sitting after a comma, where an example indicator would usually live.
explanation.definitionFit: say -> PUT: to put something well is to say it in a particular way, as in 'how would you put it?'

clue.text: Talkative dear has answer for everything, initially

indicators.note: 'X for Y' is how a swap gets announced: the first letter takes over the place the second one was holding
doing something initially means at the very outset, so only the opening letter of the word counts

blocks.note: dear means costly, not beloved — and this is the word that gets altered
A is the standard abbreviation for answer, and it is the letter moving in
the opening letter of everything is the one being turned out

explanation.walkthrough: A whole nine-letter word arrives almost intact and one vowel changes hands, which is why the clue feels too short for its answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An expansive host opens up and talks freely, a sense of the word quite separate from taking up room.

clue.text: Crumbly sandwich without filling worth getting unwrapped?

indicators.note: unwrapping takes the covering off both ends and hands you what was inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters are the bread of the word
strip the W and the H off the ends and this is the middle that is left

explanation.walkthrough: Every instruction here is disguised as something done to food, which is the whole reason none of them reads as an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbly -> SHORT: pastry with a high proportion of fat is called short because it crumbles instead of stretching, a baker's sense of the word.

clue.text: What might be left inside hat after opening of sutures?

definitions.text: What might be left inside hat after opening of sutures?

indicators.note: something inside a thing sits within it, so these letters go into the middle of the piece named beside them
what comes after follows on, so this piece is added behind the letter already found
the opening of a word is where it begins, so you take the single letter it starts with

blocks.note: only the first letter of sutures is wanted
a cap is a hat, and it opens up between its second and third letters
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.walkthrough: Read once it is an operating theatre; read again it is three pieces of shorthand. Both readings use the same words, which is what makes it an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads as a description: cut the sutures of the skull and the scalp is what a hat would still be covering.

clue.text: Land transaction only includes one mistake

indicators.note: what a thing includes it holds within itself, so the next letters go inside rather than after

blocks.note: a sale is the transaction, and it splits after its first letter
I is the Roman numeral for one
to err is to make a mistake
'one' does the work of 'only' — your one hope is your only hope

explanation.walkthrough: The two number words are a deliberate tangle: the one that says 'only' becomes a number, and the one that says 'one' becomes a Roman numeral instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Land -> SIERRA LEONE: the general word standing in for one particular West African republic, a definition by example.

clue.text: Keep stunning shot of English river

indicators.note: to get shot of something is to be rid of it, so the letter named next is thrown out of the assembly

blocks.note: to stun someone is to amaze them
'keep' plus a verb is that verb plus 'on' — keep going is go on — so it follows rather than leads
E is the abbreviation for English, and this is the letter got rid of

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a castle and 'stunning shot' like a photograph. The step that unlocks it is hearing 'keep stunning' as an instruction to carry on amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: river -> AMAZON: the plain word pointing at the great South American waterway, a definition by example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Vicar's patch has rip that needs fixing

indicators.note: anything needing repair is broken, and broken letters cannot be relied on to stay in the order they arrived in

blocks.note: the six letters of HAS RIP, reset in a new order

explanation.walkthrough: A torn cassock and a vicar make one continuous picture, so nothing announces itself as a mechanism — and the fodder hides in two of the commonest words in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicar's patch -> PARISH: the district a vicar has charge of, with 'patch' the informal word for the ground anyone covers.

clue.text: Remove stones from pockets, reversing element of race strategy

indicators.note: reversing sends a thing the other way, so the letters just found are read from the last one back to the first

blocks.note: to pit a cherry is to take the stone out of it
a snooker player who pockets a ball pots it

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves of the wordplay are verbs pretending to be a sentence about theft, and the enumeration 3,4 is the first hint that the answer belongs on a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: When to come in for fresh tyres is the tactical call a team plans a whole race around, and that stop is made in the pits.

clue.text: Dog starts to learn Italian, answering "heel" there?

indicators.note: the start of a word is the letter it opens with, and this asks for the starts of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: a pug is a small flat-faced dog
the three words hand over their opening letters in order

explanation.walkthrough: 'There' has no country in front of it: the only Italy in the clue is one of the words being taken apart, so the definition leans on the wordplay for its own subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is shaped like a boot and the region forming its heel is Puglia, so the map is what does the defining.

clue.text: Chat GPT's creator runs outside

blocks.note: OpenAI is the company that built ChatGPT
R is how a cricket scorer writes runs

explanation.walkthrough: Splitting 'Chat GPT' into two words is the misdirection: its creator turns out to be a name lifted whole into the grid rather than a person to identify.
explanation.definitionFit: outside -> OPEN-AIR: anything happening out of doors is described as open-air, the adjective for a concert or a swimming pool.

clue.text: Pump beginning to generate trickle of water

indicators.note: a beginning is where a word starts, so its opening letter is all that is taken

blocks.note: just the opening letter of generate
a rill is a small stream, the word poets use for a trickle

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is plumbing from end to end and both halves of the wordplay play along; the definition is the interrogation-room sense of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pump -> GRILL: to pump someone for information and to grill them are the same interrogation, one image from a well and one from a fire.

clue.text: The Spanish aristocrat does sweet decorations for funeral

definitions.note: 'Funeral' is singular and names the occasion; the answer is the plural set of rites performed at one, and English never puts it in the singular.

blocks.note: las is Spanish for 'the' in front of a plural
a toff is a member of the upper classes
to ice a cake is to give it its sweet decoration

explanation.walkthrough: Spanish has four words for 'the' and only the feminine plural fits; the cake-and-party surface is what keeps you from seeing where the answer is heading.
explanation.definitionFit: funeral -> LAST OFFICES: the offices are church services, and the last of them are the rites said over the dead.

clue.text: Different from gold, debt instruments reportedly untrustworthy

blocks.note: different from a thing is simply not that thing
or is the heraldic tincture gold, and a crossword staple
an IOU is a written promise to pay, so several are IOUs

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a market report and every piece plays along with it. OR for gold comes from heraldry and is worth banking — it turns up constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is a reputation rather than a fact, so the word says what people report about someone and not what is true.

clue.text: Plain bothies in disrepair providing no shelter

indicators.note: something in disrepair has fallen apart, and letters that have fallen apart can be set down again in any order

blocks.note: the twelve letters of PLAIN BOTHIES, rebuilt

explanation.walkthrough: A bothy is a rough hut kept unlocked for walkers in the Scottish hills, which is exactly what makes the surface hang together and the definition sting.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhospitable coast gives a traveller nothing to get out of the weather in, so the word describes terrain and not a rude host.

clue.text: Advert claiming merit so inappropriately paid off

indicators.note: to claim a thing is to take it in as your own, so these letters close around whatever comes next
done inappropriately means not in the proper way, and letters not in their proper way are out of order

blocks.note: ad is the everyday short form of advert, and it splits to take the rest inside
the seven letters of MERIT SO in a new order

explanation.walkthrough: A mortise is the slot a tenon fits into — a joiner's word worth keeping — and the surface is busy pretending to be a boastful advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: paid off -> AMORTISED: a loan is amortised when it has been written down to nothing by instalments, the accountant's word for clearing a debt.

clue.text: Boxing match interrupted by supporter after Fury's face puffed up

indicators.note: an interruption cuts in part-way through, so what follows lands in the middle rather than alongside
what comes after something follows it, so this piece is written below the letter just named
a face is the front of a thing, so the front letter of the name beside it is what you take

blocks.note: a bout is a boxing match, and it splits three letters in
only the front letter of the boxer's name
a fan is a supporter of a team or a fighter

explanation.walkthrough: Tyson Fury is a real heavyweight and the surface belongs entirely to him, which is why nothing in it looks like it could be about hairdressing.
explanation.definitionFit: puffed up -> BOUFFANT: a bouffant is hair backcombed into height and volume, so the answer names a shape rather than a mood.

clue.text: Classical dish Chinese-American lawyer served up

indicators.note: 'up' is the direction of travel, and in a down entry that means reading the letters from the bottom back to the top

blocks.note: Sino- is the combining form for Chinese, as in Sino-Soviet
a DA is a district attorney, the prosecuting lawyer in an American court

explanation.walkthrough: The surface promises a menu and 'served up' plays along with it; the only cookery in the clue is the direction the letters travel.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Dish' is slang for a good-looking person, and Adonis is the Greek myth's name for male beauty, so 'classical' places him.

clue.text: Orbiter going round Mars, perhaps carrying oxygen tank

indicators.note: whatever is carrying a thing holds it inside, so the letter beside it goes within rather than after

blocks.note: a comet orbits the sun on a long loop
anything that is going is on — an engine, a light, a show
a round is a circle, and O is the crossword's circle
Mars is one of the Roman gods, and 'perhaps' says he is an example of one
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, and it goes inside

explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration is the misdirection: 4,2,2,4 cuts the letters in three places the wordplay never uses. And Mars here is a Roman god, not the planet an orbiter would visit.
explanation.definitionFit: tank -> COME TO NO GOOD: to tank is to fail badly, and anything that comes to nothing has ended in exactly that failure.

clue.text: DIY sale clearing odd bits with kitchen furniture?

indicators.note: clearing out the odd ones leaves the even ones, so the first, third, fifth and seventh letters all go

blocks.note: dIySaLe hands over its second, fourth and sixth letters
and does the job of with — fish and chips is fish with chips

explanation.walkthrough: 'DIY sale' reads as a bargain hunt and is really just seven letters to count through; the question mark owns up to the definition naming one kind among many.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-standing unit marooned in the middle of the floor takes its name from the shape it makes on the plan.

clue.text: Crawl from Krakow to Warsaw

indicators.note: 'from' marks where the letters are drawn from, and the run of them starts inside the first city name and ends inside the second

blocks.note: the run begins three letters from the end of Krakow and stops on the first letter of Warsaw

explanation.walkthrough: A journey across Poland is a handsome cover for a word English took from the Chinese court, where the bow touched the forehead to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To kowtow is to abase yourself before someone, and crawling to a boss is the English idiom for the same servility.

clue.text: In a sense, the way force offer resistance

indicators.note: putting a thing in something buries it, so these letters land within the word beside them rather than after it

blocks.note: sight is one of the five senses, and it opens up after its first letter
the way you did it is how you did it
F is the physicist's symbol for force

explanation.walkthrough: 'In a sense' reads as a hedge and is really an instruction plus a noun — one of the five senses — and the comma the setter drops after it is what sells the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To show fight is to make it plain you will not go quietly, an old idiom for putting up resistance rather than folding.

clue.text: Male gymnast's head breaks weak beam

indicators.note: the head of a word is the letter it starts with, so only that one letter joins the mix
something broken has come apart, and letters that have come apart can be set down in any order

blocks.note: MALE, plus the G that heads gymnast, rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: Nothing marks 'Male' as material rather than description, which is what makes it hide so well; and a gymnast's head here is a letter, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is the faintest showing of light, so the definition fixes the strength as much as the kind.

clue.text: Slightly charming son leaves ego at home

indicators.note: when something leaves it is no longer there, so that letter drops out of the word it was sitting in

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son, and it is what departs
your ego is your self, and with that S gone this is what remains
someone at home is in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slightly' is not a hedge here but a build: slight means small and slender, which is half of what the definition is claiming.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes a small, delicately pretty look, so 'slightly' is the slenderness of it and 'charming' the appeal.

clue.text: Diplomat not drinking gripped by advanced thirst

indicators.note: whatever grips a thing has closed around it, so these letters end up held inside the others

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in an A-level
TT is teetotal, the usual shorthand for someone off the drink
an ache for something is a longing, which is what a thirst for it is

explanation.walkthrough: Every piece is a standing abbreviation dressed as description, and 'advanced thirst' is written as one phrase precisely so that you will not split it.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomat -> ATTACHE: an attache is a junior specialist on an embassy staff, so the general word names one particular rank.

clue.text: Better teacher said "Ask me another"

indicators.note: 'said' means the words are being spoken, so you write down the sound of them rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a schoolmaster is addressed as sir, and out loud that becomes the opening syllable
pass is what you say on a quiz show when you cannot answer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' at the front is a verb rather than a comparison, and the quoted phrase is the sound of a contestant giving up on a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Better -> SURPASS: to better a rival is to go one past them, which is what surpassing is — both are verbs of exceeding.

clue.text: Go off summit in the wrong direction

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling from the far end back, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, the Dartmoor word crosswords lean on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' is the kitchen sense of the phrase, not the departing one — and a summit turned round is the shortest kind of reversal there is.
explanation.definitionFit: Go off -> ROT: food that goes off has begun to rot, so the phrasal verb and the plain one name the same decay.

clue.text: Upland swallows

definitions.note: The answer is a plural name for a stretch of country, while 'Upland' is the singular word for the kind of country it is — the Downs are never spoken of singly.

blocks.note: the chalk hills of southern England, from an old word meaning hill
to down a pint is to swallow it in one

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that look like opposites sit side by side, up in the clue and down in the answer, and that contradiction is the whole of the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The Downs are the chalk uplands of southern England, and to down a drink is to swallow it — hill country and gulping in one word.

clue.text: Consider change to script that bores friend

indicators.note: to bore into something is to drive right through the middle of it, so these letters end up inside

blocks.note: a mate is a friend, and it splits after its first letter
to edit a script is to change it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' is doing work rather than commentary: it drills a hole through the middle of a word instead of sending anyone to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Consider -> MEDITATE: to meditate on a problem is to turn it over at length, so the answer is considering done slowly and deliberately.
